text:
For most of two periods in Newark, the Devils were playing the kind of game that gets everyone home early. Then they gave up three goals in just over three minutes of the third, and needed a Connor Hellebuyck save and Jesper Bratt's finish to get out with a 5-4 overtime win over St. Louis.

Before the wobble, it was a showcase. Luke Hughes opened the scoring at 7:34 of the first with his brother Jack on the assist, and New Jersey owned that period, out-chancing the Blues 1.58 to 0.49 in expected goals. Anthony Mantha made it 2-0 in the second on a 79% chance. Robert Thomas got one back on the power play, but Jesper Boqvist and Mantha scored 19 seconds apart late in the period for a 4-1 lead.

Mantha finished with two goals and an assist in 13:36, and his own chances were worth 1.72 expected goals, the most of anyone on the ice. Overall the Devils generated 6.59 expected goals to 4.04; replay every shot and they win this game 83% of the time. Jordan Binnington is the reason it was ever close. He saved 1.6 goals more than his 36 shots against deserved.

Then the third. Mason McTavish scored at 11:46. Philip Broberg beat Hellebuyck at 14:36 on a 4% chance, the least likely goal of the night, and Dalibor Dvorsky tipped in the tying goal 18 seconds later. The Blues had a 12% chance to win before Dvorsky's tip and 48% after it, and you could forgive a Devils fan for wondering where the last 20 minutes went.

Overtime nearly went the wrong way too. Twenty-nine seconds in, Hellebuyck stopped McTavish on a 42% look, the best chance anyone missed all night and the biggest save of the game. A minute later Bratt took a Dougie Hamilton feed and finished a 69% chance at 1:26. That makes three straight wins for New Jersey, and the process behind this one was excellent. The third period is the part they'll want to watch twice, and then never again.
headline: Devils blow a three-goal lead, then Bratt ends it
